title: cov2corr
summary: Convert a covariance matrix to a correlation matrix.

gpu_support.notes: Resident real gpuArray covariance matrices are a RunMat extension. An available provider `covariance_to_correlation` hook returns resident standard-deviation and correlation outputs; unsupported providers use the host reference path.

description: `ExpSigma = cov2corr(ExpCovariance)` returns a 1-by-n row of standard deviations. `[ExpSigma,ExpCorrC] = cov2corr(ExpCovariance)` also returns the n-by-n correlation matrix. The output order and shape follow the Finance Toolbox API and differ from `corrcov`.
behaviors: The documented Finance Toolbox input is a real double square covariance matrix. RunMat mode also accepts real single, typed-integer, and logical inputs; scalar numeric inputs are treated as 1-by-1 matrices.
The diagonal entries of `C` are interpreted as variances and must be nonnegative.
RunMat validates symmetry within floating-point tolerance before converting.
RunMat rejects covariance entries whose magnitude exceeds the variance-implied pairwise bound `sqrt(C(i,i)*C(j,j))`.
Entries involving a zero-variance variable produce `NaN` because the correlation denominator is zero.
The first output is a row vector of standard deviations. The second is the correlation matrix; this is not an alias for `corrcov`.
Resident real gpuArray input is a RunMat extension and stays resident when the active provider implements covariance-to-correlation conversion.

faqs.question: Is `cov2corr` different from `corrcov`?
faqs.answer: Yes. `cov2corr` returns standard deviations first as a row and the correlation matrix second. `corrcov` returns correlation first and standard deviations second as a column.
